style.name: Warm Oilcloth Family
style.style_notes: Paint each creature as something loved: broad, flat color, sincere eyes and a slight wobble in the edge. Keep marks few and steady between frames. Dark paint belongs inside the creature; the surrounding cell stays clear. Glass keeps its clear heart and soft rim, while ink gives solid bodies their weight. Warmth comes from care, not a shine added to everything.
style.framing: Use transparent 192 × 208 cells. Keep every pose inside x=16–176 and y=16–192, with standing feet or body base at y=184. Reserve room above for jumps and beside the body for waves. Fit tall creatures by gently bending their posture, keeping their defining shape. Lock scale, face placement and carried objects across frames. Each row has 16 frames at 8 fps: two seconds, four beats of four frames. Repeat held drawings within that grid. Keep motion within the cell; movement across the screen belongs to the player. One-shot rows finish in a stable pose. Idle and waiting use small movements and long holds.
style.palette: Core paint: soot #262321, cream #F1DFC1, ochre #C59A46, rust #AC5740, herb green #65764C and blue #557589. Preserve each seed's own colors: the trolleybus stays blue, the ram gold, the ermine white and the droplet clear. Lights stay within their existing flame, lantern, window or body. V2 adds sixteen selectable looks to the base sheet, each covering all nine rows and all twenty seeds. These change paint handling and small accents, never creature, costume or props: 1. Dry Paint—sparse broad grain; 2. Full Paint—solid matte fills; 3. Thin Paint—slightly translucent fills; 4. Broken Edge—small fixed gaps in solid-body outlines; 5. Soft Edge—gentler edge transitions; 6. Firm Edge—clearer shape boundaries; 7. Cream Edge—a narrow light-facing rim; 8. Soot Edge—a deeper inward border; 9. Ochre Touch—ochre on existing small accents; 10. Rust Touch—rust on existing small accents; 11. Herb Touch—green on existing small accents; 12. Blue Touch—blue on existing small accents; 13. Pale Paint—lighter secondary colors; 14. Deep Paint—darker secondary colors; 15. Quiet Paint—less saturated secondary colors; 16. Fresh Paint—stronger secondary colors. Protect identity colors and face contrast in every look. Glass variants affect rim softness, tint or inner light only; its center remains clear.
style.line: Solid bodies use irregular ink edges about 3 pixels wide, with essential inner marks at least 2 pixels wide. Keep important gaps at least 4 pixels open. Suggest texture with a few broad marks fixed to the body, never changing noise. The glass droplet is the deliberate exception: use a broad, soft, partly open rim and a clear center, without a hard black enclosure. The magnifying glass has an ink frame and a clear lens. Family likeness comes from shared proportions, restraint and timing, rather than forcing glass to become opaque ink.
style.boundaries: All twenty seeds remain themselves. Keep the magnifying glass's raised eyebrow and searching tilt; the ram's gold fleece, herb sprig and attached twig that greens with happiness; the hut's chicken legs, kerchief roof and door broom; the sleepy mushroom's moss, tarragon and herb basket; the crescent's lantern; the still white ermine's distinct frost crown; the bold calf's embroidered felt blanket and hoof stamp; the book's flapping covers and changing ink pictures; the determined brush's legs and paint jar; the thoughtful inkpot's spectacles and tucked quill; the quiet palette's paint spots and brush tail; the curled lamb's striped cap and candle; the calm clear droplet; the gentle giraffe's long neck and sincere eyes; the precise bee's white collar and pressed flower; the generous pomegranate's opening rind and visible seeds; the courteous wooden soldier's back key and salute; the tuning fork's poised turns; the blue trolleybus's warm windows and guitar visible on its seat; and the clay lamp's grapevine handle. Use new poses, markings and patterns. Existing belongings remain attached, held or securely contained. Do not add shared herbs, keys, lamps, costumes or ornaments to other seeds. Sweeping leaves no footprint marks; frost appears only on the crown or feet; underlining and writing become small gestures without drawn words; shared seeds stay cupped in the open rind. Humming and ringing read through posture without sound symbols. No floating effects, scene background, text, speech bubbles, shadows or new review props. Review uses only the creature and its existing belongings. All pets and sheets remain local. Paul waived approval steps and retains a later veto.

rows.idle: Beat 1: settled pose. Beat 2: one slow blink or slight head dip. Beat 3: a 1–2 pixel breath. Beat 4: return and hold. Keep sleepy pets curled, proud pets upright and the palette quietly seated. Loop gently.
rows.running-right: Face right. Beat 1: first contact. Beat 2: lift and pass. Beat 3: opposite contact. Beat 4: lift and return. Legs stride, wheels turn, covers or bee wings beat; legless bodies tip and bob along the same pulse. Keep carried objects secure.
rows.running-left: Use the same four-beat travel cycle facing left. Redraw the turn so the eyebrow, herbs, quill, broom, guitar and other uneven details remain attached to their proper places. Do not simply mirror the finished sheet.
rows.waving: Beat 1: turn toward the viewer. Beat 2: raise an available limb, cover, branch or body edge. Beat 3: make one clear greeting sweep. Beat 4: lower and settle. Bodies without limbs tilt in greeting. Keep held flames and jars upright. Play once.
rows.jumping: Beat 1: crouch or compress. Beat 2: rise 10–14 pixels. Beat 3: reach the peak and descend. Beat 4: land, soften and settle. Winged pets use a brief upward flap; the trolleybus gives a small springy hop. Show no trails or landing marks. Play once.
rows.failed: Beat 1: stop abruptly. Beat 2: sink or tilt downward. Beat 3: hold a plainly disappointed pose. Beat 4: recover slightly while keeping the lowered gaze. No damage or comic panic. Play once and hold; this must differ from a sleepy idle.
rows.waiting: Beat 1: look toward the expected action. Beat 2: hold. Beat 3: make one restrained questioning tilt or weight shift. Beat 4: hold with eyes open. The calf may make one small hoof press. Existing lights stay steady. Loop without pacing.
rows.running: This means a task is active, not travel. Stay planted and lean toward the work. Beat 1: prepare. Beat 2: act. Beat 3: check. Beat 4: reset. The hut sweeps close to its feet, the brush works at its own jar rim, the inkpot traces an empty underline gesture, the book turns a pictured page and the magnifier scans. Other seeds use focused body motions with their existing belongings. Loop.
rows.review: Beat 1: become still and attentive. Beat 2: inspect an existing body detail or belonging, or turn thoughtfully when there is none. Beat 3: hold the considered pose. Beat 4: give one small nod and settle. The magnifier angles its lens inward; the palette studies a paint dab. Keep the motion small and distinct from the broad greeting. Add nothing. Play once.

style.why: I want each pet to look cared for, with its own work and temper still visible. The dark oilcloth feeling lives in the painted body and can meet a dark app surface without baking a background into the sprite. No veto is proposed. Originality may veto only in a jury and never ranks taste. The Painter checks function at native size across all nine rows and sixteen added looks. Any function flag must name the pet, look, row and frame, and describe visible evidence such as a vanished eyebrow, a clipped crown or two actions with the same silhouette. These are checks to perform, not defects claimed without images. Any later charter veto must quote the exact guards-against line and give a concrete reason.

brief.description: A quiet bee with a tiny white collar and one pressed flower; a single careful gesture says enough.
brief.brief:
Hem is a small bee who carries a pressed flower as carefully as a letter. Its round ochre body has broad soot bands, cream wings and a tiny white collar with two clear points. The flower is flat rust paint on a short herb-green stem, always held close. A slight unevenness in the ink edge makes the bee feel handled and loved.

Quiet does not mean absent. Hem notices, chooses and acts. Its eyes are sincere; its forelegs move with care. Pleasure lifts the head a little. Doubt sends the gaze outward. Failure folds the posture inward, then leaves enough strength for another try. Nothing becomes frantic or grand.

Its signature is one short writing stroke with a free foreleg, a pause to judge the thought, then flight when travel begins. The stroke leaves no words or marks and needs no pen. The pressed flower stays secure in the other forelegs.

Let the collar and flower carry the meaning. Keep paint broad, texture sparse and fixed, and all dark edges within the creature. Waiting reaches toward an expected event; work makes the stroke; review brings the flower toward the face. These whole-body differences must survive the small cell. Add no ornaments, loose pollen, floating effects, background, text, speech bubbles, shadows or new review props.
brief.pet_notes: Use a compact oval body, two broad soot bands and a warm ochre face. Keep the tiny collar truly white, with its points separated from the cream wings. Two short antennae frame clear dark eyes. The pressed flower has one simple rust head and a short green stem. Give the limbs enough width to read; keep the flower held and its shape steady.

rows.idle: Across 6 frames, rest upright with the flower low against the body, blink once, breathe slightly and return to the same quiet hold.
rows.running-right: Across 8 frames, face right with a forward flight lean and clear alternating wing positions, holding the flower securely while remaining inside the cell.
rows.running-left: Across 8 frames, redraw the bee facing left through the same flight pulse, preserving the flower's grip and the collar's structure rather than mirroring the finished drawings.
rows.waving: Across 4 frames, face the viewer, lift the free foreleg, sweep it once in greeting and lower it while the flower stays held.
rows.jumping: Across 5 frames, compress, flap upward about 10–14 pixels, reach the peak, descend and settle without trails or landing marks.
rows.failed: Across 8 frames, stop, lower the head and antennae, fold the free foreleg inward, hold disappointment and recover slightly with the gaze still down.
rows.waiting: Across 6 frames, keep the flower low, lean toward the expected action with open eyes and forward antennae, make one questioning tilt and hold without writing.
rows.running: Across 6 frames, stay planted, brace the flower against the chest, extend the free foreleg through one short writing gesture, check its endpoint and reset without leaving a mark.
rows.review: Across 6 frames, raise the held flower toward the face, incline the whole body to inspect its flattened head, hold, nod once and lower it into a stable pose.

do_not_resemble: No franchise look-alike, logo, real-person likeness or copied artwork.
brief.why: Emily's choice is the white collar beside one pressed flower: two small details carry care and restraint. I assume the flower needs no backing paper and writing is a bare foreleg gesture; neither adds a prop. Flight belongs to travel, keeping focused work planted. The v2 contract replaces the sheet's conflicting frame grid and paint variants: one local transparent 1536 × 2288 atlas, eight columns by eleven rows of 192 × 208 cells; rows 0–8 use 6, 8, 8, 4, 5, 8, 6, 6 and 6 frames, with unused cells fully transparent. Rows 9–10 contain sixteen static gaze and pose directions, clockwise from up in 22.5-degree steps, with unchanged paint and palette. Head, antennae and body orientation distinguish adjacent directions. Retain 8 fps as playback guidance and adapt holds to the required counts. Keep poses within x=16–176 and y=16–192, the resting base at y=184, edges about 3 pixels, inner marks at least 2 pixels and important gaps at least 4 pixels. Apply the supplied readability lessons through distinct body and flower positions, not eye changes alone. No images were supplied for this draft, so no function defect is claimed. Only skill validators gate production; motion deviations belong in provenance. No veto is proposed; Originality only vetoes in juries and never ranks taste. Paul waived approval and retains his later veto.

previous.motion_policy: Style-sheet motion numbers (pixel displacement, angles, timing and amplitudes) are drawing guidance. Only the skill's validators gate a pet; a measured difference from style guidance is recorded in provenance, not a reason to fail or spend repairs.

decisions: All artifacts stayed local. No Pets MCP, Library, upload, creation, selection, activation, or update was performed.
The previous attempt contained no reusable art and was preserved unchanged.
Used the fixed ram reference for family style while retaining Hem’s bee identity, white collar, and pressed flower.
Generated sequentially with one art worker; copied all 19 cache sources into this attempt and logged prompts, references, source paths, hashes, and repair attempts.
Writing uses a bare foreleg without marks or extra props. Waiting reaches outward; work strokes downward while planted; review lifts the flower toward the face.
Look directions use head, eyes, and antennae around planted feet and an attached flower.
Uniform row registration used 0.70 scale for standard rows and 0.86 for jumping, with resting bases at y=184; no individual pose resizing.
Combined the complete family and standard contact sheets when needed to keep image jobs within five references.
Observed jump lift is 42 pixels versus 10–14 pixel guidance, with zero landing-baseline difference. The contained wing-assisted hop preserves the intended action.
Idle bounds vary vertically by 3 pixels versus 1–2 pixel breath guidance; the feet remain planted and the motion stays restrained.
Retained 8 fps as drawing guidance; final previews use bundled state timings and longer holds, recorded in logs/preview-export.json.
Three isolated read-only reviewers confirmed every cardinal. The 337.5° horizontal component is ambiguous in isolation and remains an explicit intermediate warning.
Two assembled candidates each received exactly one despill pass. The first failed silhouette checks; the repaired second candidate passes the bundled gates.
Nineteen imagegen calls comprise thirteen planned assets and six visual repairs. No whole-pet redo occurred.
Final output is a lossless transparent 1536×2288 WebP. Atlas, compressed contact, provenance, and QA metadata total 1,804,974 bytes.
Required reports are in qa/. Nine state GIFs, all-state GIF/MP4, idle-jump-idle GIF/MP4, look-loop GIF/MP4, contact sheets, and labeled stills are in previews/.

reasons.why: Directional look, row 10, frame 7, 337.5 degrees: the face reads nearly straight upward, with little visible leftward aim. This matches the intermediate-direction warning in the supplied context; it does not establish a reversed cardinal.
Row 10, frame 7, at 337.5°: the face reads upward and nearly frontal; the leftward component is unclear.
Row 10, frame 7, look 337.5: the bee returns to an almost frontal pose, making the leftward part of its gaze weak. The supplied blind-review summary also records that ambiguity.

readability_notes.instruction: Readability notes from the image jury: make waiting, focused work (running row 7), and review read differently from idle and from each other at 192 × 208. Apply the winning style's supplied attributed drawing notes to this pet, including the reference pet. Carry them into every image prompt. These are drawing guidance; keep the fixed family reference and the v2 contract.

flags.why: Trolleybus, base animation, review row 8 frames 1–4: blinking and small gaze changes carry most of the action while the body and guitar remain still. Inspection is difficult to distinguish from idle. Running/work row 7 frames 1–2 shows concentration, but the work itself is unclear.

Trolleybus, base look: review row 8, frames 0–5, mainly shows eye changes and a closing smile. Inspection of the seated guitar is not clearly readable; frames 0–3 remain close to idle. This is a state-readability concern, not a charter veto.
Ram, directional looks: row 10, frames 5–7 (292.5–337.5), show closely similar upward head turns. The broad direction reads, but the separate steps are weak.
Trolleybus, base look: review row 8, frames 1–4, relies on small eye changes and a blink much like idle row 0, frames 1–3. Inspection of the seated guitar is hard to read.

Trolleybus, base treatment: review row 8, frames 0–5, mostly shows forward attention and blinking, much like idle row 0. The intended inspection of the seated guitar is not clear in the supplied drawings.

Bulat, base look, running row 7, frames 1–2: lowered eyebrows show concentration, but the seated guitar shows no clear working action. Review row 8, frames 1–5 reads mostly as looking and blinking. Work and inspection are weakly distinguished.
Medea, base look, running row 7 and review row 8, frames 1–4: both use head dips toward the mouth-held herbs. The separate act, check and inspect beats are difficult to distinguish.

contract:
The v2 sprite-sheet contract fixes 192 × 208 cells, eight columns by eleven rows,
one transparent 1536 × 2288 atlas. The nine animation rows (0–8) have these exact frame counts:
idle 6, running-right 8, running-left 8, waving 4, jumping 5, failed 8, waiting 6,
running 6 (focused work, not locomotion), review 6. Unused cells stay fully transparent.
Rows 9 and 10 hold sixteen look directions, eight per row, clockwise in screen coordinates:
row 9: 000, 022.5, 045, 067.5, 090, 112.5, 135, 157.5;
row 10: 180, 202.5, 225, 247.5, 270, 292.5, 315, 337.5.
000 is up, 090 right, 180 down, 270 left. These are gaze/pose directions with the same
palette and treatment, not sixteen palette variants, paint treatments or separate animations.
motion_policy: Style-sheet motion numbers (pixel displacement, angles, timing and amplitudes) are drawing guidance. Only the skill's validators gate a pet; a measured difference from style guidance is recorded in provenance, not a reason to fail or spend repairs.

contract_overrides.original: Each row has 16 frames at 8 fps: two seconds, four beats of four frames. Repeat held drawings within that grid.
contract_overrides.replacement: Rows 0–8 contain 6,8,8,4,5,8,6,6,6 frames. Remap four beats to those counts, with 8 fps playback guidance (125 ms per frame); durations are 0.75,1,1,0.5,0.625,1,0.75,0.75,0.75 seconds.
contract_overrides.reason: The v2 contract fixes frame counts; retain the four-beat intent.

contract_overrides.original: V2 adds sixteen selectable looks to the base sheet, each covering all nine rows and all twenty seeds. These change paint handling and small accents, never creature, costume or props: 1. Dry Paint—sparse broad grain; 2. Full Paint—solid matte fills; 3. Thin Paint—slightly translucent fills; 4. Broken Edge—small fixed gaps in solid-body outlines; 5. Soft Edge—gentler edge transitions; 6. Firm Edge—clearer shape boundaries; 7. Cream Edge—a narrow light-facing rim; 8. Soot Edge—a deeper inward border; 9. Ochre Touch—ochre on existing small accents; 10. Rust Touch—rust on existing small accents; 11. Herb Touch—green on existing small accents; 12. Blue Touch—blue on existing small accents; 13. Pale Paint—lighter secondary colors; 14. Deep Paint—darker secondary colors; 15. Quiet Paint—less saturated secondary colors; 16. Fresh Paint—stronger secondary colors. Protect identity colors and face contrast in every look. Glass variants affect rim softness, tint or inner light only; its center remains clear.
contract_overrides.replacement: Rows 9 and 10 contain sixteen static gaze/pose directions clockwise from up: 000,022.5,045,067.5,090,112.5,135,157.5; 180,202.5,225,247.5,270,292.5,315,337.5. Preserve one unchanged palette and broad matte painterly treatment throughout.
contract_overrides.reason: V2 looks are directions, not paint variants or additional animation sheets.

contract_overrides.original: Beat 1: settled pose. Beat 2: one slow blink or slight head dip. Beat 3: a 1–2 pixel breath. Beat 4: return and hold. Keep sleepy pets curled, proud pets upright and the palette quietly seated. Loop gently.
contract_overrides.replacement: 6 frames; beats 1/2/3/4 occupy frames 0; 1–2; 3–4; 5. Rest upright with the flower low, blink once, breathe slightly, and return.
contract_overrides.reason: Remap four beats to the required frame count; motion amplitudes remain guidance.

contract_overrides.original: Face right. Beat 1: first contact. Beat 2: lift and pass. Beat 3: opposite contact. Beat 4: lift and return. Legs stride, wheels turn, covers or bee wings beat; legless bodies tip and bob along the same pulse. Keep carried objects secure.
contract_overrides.replacement: 8 frames; beats occupy 0–1; 2–3; 4–5; 6–7. Face right with alternating flight wing positions and a securely held flower.
contract_overrides.reason: Remap the travel cycle to eight frames.

contract_overrides.original: Use the same four-beat travel cycle facing left. Redraw the turn so the eyebrow, herbs, quill, broom, guitar and other uneven details remain attached to their proper places. Do not simply mirror the finished sheet.
contract_overrides.replacement: 8 frames; beats occupy 0–1; 2–3; 4–5; 6–7. Independently generate leftward flight, preserving the flower grip and collar.
contract_overrides.reason: Meet the v2 count while preserving asymmetric construction.

contract_overrides.original: Beat 1: turn toward the viewer. Beat 2: raise an available limb, cover, branch or body edge. Beat 3: make one clear greeting sweep. Beat 4: lower and settle. Bodies without limbs tilt in greeting. Keep held flames and jars upright. Play once.
contract_overrides.replacement: 4 frames; beats occupy 0; 1; 2; 3. Face the viewer, raise the free foreleg, greet, and settle with the flower held.
contract_overrides.reason: One frame per beat meets the v2 count.

contract_overrides.original: Beat 1: crouch or compress. Beat 2: rise 10–14 pixels. Beat 3: reach the peak and descend. Beat 4: land, soften and settle. Winged pets use a brief upward flap; the trolleybus gives a small springy hop. Show no trails or landing marks. Play once.
contract_overrides.replacement: 5 frames; beats occupy 0; 1; 2–3; 4. Compress, rise, peak, descend, and settle. Retain 10–14 pixels as drawing guidance.
contract_overrides.reason: Preserve anticipation, airborne motion, and landing within five frames.

contract_overrides.original: Beat 1: stop abruptly. Beat 2: sink or tilt downward. Beat 3: hold a plainly disappointed pose. Beat 4: recover slightly while keeping the lowered gaze. No damage or comic panic. Play once and hold; this must differ from a sleepy idle.
contract_overrides.replacement: 8 frames; beats occupy 0–1; 2–3; 4–5; 6–7. Lower head and antennae, fold inward, hold disappointment, and recover slightly.
contract_overrides.reason: Retain the emotional progression within eight frames.

contract_overrides.original: Beat 1: look toward the expected action. Beat 2: hold. Beat 3: make one restrained questioning tilt or weight shift. Beat 4: hold with eyes open. The calf may make one small hoof press. Existing lights stay steady. Loop without pacing.
contract_overrides.replacement: 6 frames; beats occupy 0–1; 2; 3–4; 5. Keep eyes open and flower low, lean outward, question, and hold without writing.
contract_overrides.reason: Remap the patient four-beat action to six frames.

contract_overrides.original: This means a task is active, not travel. Stay planted and lean toward the work. Beat 1: prepare. Beat 2: act. Beat 3: check. Beat 4: reset. The hut sweeps close to its feet, the brush works at its own jar rim, the inkpot traces an empty underline gesture, the book turns a pictured page and the magnifier scans. Other seeds use focused body motions with their existing belongings. Loop.
contract_overrides.replacement: 6 frames; beats occupy 0; 1–2; 3–4; 5. Stay planted, brace the flower, make one bare-foreleg writing stroke, check, and reset.
contract_overrides.reason: Meet the frame count while preserving focused work rather than locomotion.
